`add / --type header/footer --prop type=<sub-type>` to seed each part
(AddHeader/AddFooter create the part with one auto paragraph). The seed

paragraph has a single run; multi-run first paragraphs collapse to plain

fix(anthropic): strip top-level oneOf/allOf/anyOf from tool input_schema

Extends the existing _normalize_tool_input_schema to also drop top-level
union keywords that Anthropic's tool schema validator rejects with HTTP 400.

Several upstream and plugin tools ship schemas with a top-level oneOf/
allOf/anyOf (common for Pydantic discriminated unions). The existing
strip_nullable_unions pass only handles anyOf-with-null patterns; a
non-null top-level union keyword sails through and hits the API.

fix(indexer): strip MULTIPLE metadata headers in single message

Root cause: Telegram messages have BOTH 'Conversation info' AND 'Sender' metadata blocks:
  'Conversation info (untrusted metadata): \n\nSender (untrusted metadata): \n\n[actual content]'

Previous code only stripped ONE prefix, leaving the second one to be detected as noise.

Fix: _strip_metadata_headers() now uses a loop to strip ALL metadata prefixes iteratively, with a safety limit of 5 iterations.

fix(e2e): restore exec in start-gateway.sh — tee pipe broke process management

The tee pipe (without exec) made the shell script the parent process,
not the gateway. When Playwright kills the shell, the gateway becomes
an orphan still holding the port. The next test retry starts a new
gateway that can't fully initialize because the orphan is still
running. This caused chat-abort and chat-api-message RPC timeouts.

Restored exec so Playwright manages the gateway process directly.

shell-quoting bug: JSON.stringify wraps in double quotes with embedded
\" escapes, which the shell un-escapes when expanding the outer
double-quoted -e argument. The shell ends up parsing the script with
broken quote nesting.

Restructure the script as:
  1. cat > /tmp/manifest.json   (consumes kubectl stdin; closes on EOF)
  2. node - /tmp/manife

v5.0.7: drop sha256_batch Rust dispatch in compression contest store

The compression-commit-hash call site is naturally one-payload-at-a-
time, so routing it through mnemos_hot.sha256_batch added FFI
marshalling cost without a batching benefit. hashlib.sha256 already
wraps OpenSSL in C with the GIL released, so a direct call is at
least as fast and removes ~25 lines of fallback indirection. The
mnemos_hot wheel still exposes sha256_batch for any future caller
that genuinely batches.

fix: correct order of decipher.update() and decipher.final() in decryptSecret

The AES-256-GCM decryption was calling decipher.final() BEFORE
decipher.update(ciphertext), which caused the auth tag validation to
fail because the ciphertext hadn't been processed yet.

修复: 思考过程结束后默认折叠并展示思考时长 (#493)

关闭 #493。

## 问题描述
Web 端 Agent 流式输出的「思考过程」区域在思考阶段结束后整块从 UI 中消失，
最终回复出现时下方内容向上跳动，且用户失去回看 Agent 推理过程的入口。

## 修复方案
对齐主流 LLM 产品（ChatGPT / Claude）的折叠模式：
思考阶段结束（isThinking: true → false）时自动把 Reasoning 块从展开
切换为折叠，标题改为「已思考 X 秒」。同一 Reasoning 块在 StreamingDisplay
和 MessageBubble 之间高度一致，最终回复抵达时不再产生跳变。
用户可以点击折叠条重新展开查看完整思考内容。如果用户在本轮已经手动
切换过展开状态，则保留用户选择不再自动折叠。

### `web/src/stores/chat.ts`
- StreamingState 新增 `thinkingStartedAt` / `thinkingDurationMs`
- 在 thinking_delta 首次到达时记录起始时

OpenShell now handles TLS termination automatically for REST endpoints,

warnings on policy reload. This removes those deprecated directives from
the base policy and built-in presets while keeping the existing `tls:
skip` entries for WebSocket pass-through endpoints.

fix(tui): call process.exit(0) after Ink exit to trigger terminal cleanup

Ink's exit() calls unmount() which resets terminal modes (kitty keyboard,
mouse, etc.) but does NOT call process.exit().  The Node process stays
alive because stdin is still open (Ink listens on it), so the
process.on('exit') handler in entry.tsx — which sends the final
resetTerminalModes() — never fires.

This left kitty keyboard protocol and other terminal modes enabled in the
parent shell after /quit, Ctrl+C, or Ctrl+D

test that asserted err != nil from agent.LoadCredentials post-logout. That
made the test pass but corrupted the on-disk semantic — a 0-byte file means
"unparseable", not "absent". Future code can't distinguish "user logged out"
from "I/O failure mid-write".

os.Stat + os.IsNotExist to verify
